title: Coherent support on the adic closed fibre is detected by the first quotient
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal, X a Noetherian scheme, p:X → Spec A and F a coherent module. Then Supp(F) intersect p inverse V(I) is contained in Supp(F/(I O_X)F).

proof.text: Reuse Scheme.Modules.finite_stalk_from_affine from FiniteTypeModuleSupportPullback through a proof-only import all; do not reprove finite-type restriction or finite stalk generation. For K = I O_X and x in K.support, represent a stalk ideal element on an affine neighbourhood. The ideal support criterion shows its germ is not a unit, so the stalk ideal lies in the maximal ideal. The ideal-module-product stalk theorem identifies the first quotient stalk with F_x/K_x F_x. If this quotient is zero, its defining submodule is the whole finite stalk. Nakayama then makes that stalk zero, contradicting membership in Supp(F). Finally support_comap, coe_support_ofIdealTop and Spec_zeroLocus identify K.support with p inverse V(I).
